ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the x-axis at point $A(-3,0)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$ represents the range of the independent variable $x$ when $y>0$, \\
therefore, from the graph in the question, it indicates the range of the coordinate $x$ where the graph of the linear function is above the x-axis, \\
therefore, according to the graph in the question, when $x<-3$, the graph of the linear function is above the x-axis, \\
therefore, when $x<-3$, we have $kx+b>0$, \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{x<-3}$.
